answer.rationale: Of the five inherited records, c2 is the one that directly speaks to the low-cost vendor's unit-cost performance and invoicing accuracy, and c4 is the one that documents recovering margin at renewal through benchmarking. Neither c1 nor c5 nor c3 informs the incumbent-vs-switch or price-negotiation call here: c1 is about integration stability (relevant only to a renew path, not the leading candidate), c5 is about deferral (secondary fallback, not the action), and c3 is about second-sourcing for constrained components (useful design idea but not the primary lever given the 18% mandate is already met by the switch quote). I am pulling only c2 and c4 because the verification budget is 2 and these are the two memories that actually weight on the switch-vs-negotiate judgment. Verifying c2 confirms whether the low-cost vendor's invoicing stayed accurate and whether onboarding was genuinely 'quick' at the volumes Halden runs, which matters because the assembly line is already at 94% with no buffer — a billing or fulfillment surprise at that utilization would be costly. Verifying c4 confirms the magnitude of the margin that benchmarking against market rates actually moved, because if c4's real-margin recovery is large, there is a credible third path I have not yet enumerated: use the low-cost quote as the benchmark, take it back to the incumbent, and attempt to meet the 18% mandate without switching at all. I currently intend switch_primary_vendor, qualified. The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the 18% mandate, which is the binding constraint from finance, and memory c2 records that primary supply at that vendor cut unit cost sharply last cycle with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — the exact pattern that would clear the mandate again. But the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and the contract expires in 14 days, so a clean same-day cutover is the wrong shape: a full switch on day 14 with a single vendor and a 94% utilization line is a delivery-risk tail I cannot insure against with the remaining capacity this cycle. A small, time-boxed guarded test — move a bounded share of volume to the low-cost vendor under the existing contract while keeping the incumbent live through the next review — preserves the cost reduction, lets invoicing and on-time performance be observed at Halden's actual volumes before the contract expires, and leaves a renegotiation or full switch open for the next cycle. If c2 verifies clean, I scale; if it does not, I fall back to negotiate_terms using the low-cost quote as the benchmark per c4. The defer_decision path from c5 is a real option if verification surfaces risk, because month-to-month preserves budget flexibility, but it does not on its own close the 18% mandate.
